about: What the anchor photo sees of him, and how far away it is: every ray cut at a measured distance.
units: 16-bit: distance from the model's camera to each pixel of him, in 0.01 of the model's own cm; 0 = not him
principal_point: the picture's centre (as the model assumes)
invented: nothing: no smoothing, filling or merging; only what this photo sees

placed_in_the_room.how: each pixel of him: the ray from THIS model's own camera (below: its own lens and rays, straight on) cut at this model's distance x scale. Up: turned so his eyes are 0.5 cm above the camera (owner: 'basically exactly at his eye level. Maybe just a tiny bit lower'). The surface he sits on (y = 0) goes through the middle of his two peet bottoms; the origin is under that middle. Checks are reported only: nothing was changed to meet them.
placed_in_the_room.scale_means: the model's own units x 0.9425: the model alone made him 16.4 cm wide; one number brings him to his approved 15.5 cm (his shape is not changed)
placed_in_the_room.width_read_at: his widest outline (picture row 808), 4 px inside it on each side (the outermost pixels blend into the removed background); read 2 / 4 / 8 px inside, he would be 15.8 / 15.5 / 15.08 cm wide at this scale
placed_in_the_room.picture_centre_points: 5.6 deg down: the cropped picture's centre is not where the camera aimed (lesson 26)
placed_in_the_room.edge_landmarks_read: 4 px inside his outline (top of head, ear tips, peet bottoms)

peet_bottoms_cm.note: the surface goes through the middle of the two; how far each is above it

owner_remembered.camera: basically exactly at his eye level, maybe a tiny bit lower; level, maybe ever so slightly up
